q: Why does an expansion block of U-Net receive a copy and crop of feature maps from the matching contraction block?
options: To reduce the number of classes the network must predict
To remove duplicate bounding boxes from the output
To make up for information lost during max pooling
To convert the mask back into a single label
explain: Max pooling throws away detail on the way down. Copying and cropping the earlier feature maps hands some of that detail back so the reconstructed mask is sharper.

q: A system must find pedestrians and vehicles in video as it plays. Which approach suits this real time task?
options: Image segmentation with a mask for every frame
Object detection, for example with YOLO
Classification with one label for each frame
A bigger classifier that ignores location
explain: Detection gives faster boxes and labels, which suits real time work. A single frame label cannot say where each pedestrian or vehicle is.

q: In YOLO, which grid cell is responsible for detecting a particular object?
options: Every cell that the object touches
The cell that contains the centre of the object
The cell in the top left corner of the image
The cell with the lowest confidence score
explain: Each cell detects objects whose centre falls inside it. This is quicker than checking every possible region as R-CNN does.

q: Why is non maximum suppression applied to YOLO predictions?
options: The network produces too few boxes for each object
Several boxes can land on one object, so duplicates are removed
Pixel values must be scaled back to the range 0 to 255 before display
The confidence scores must be turned into class labels
explain: Many boxes can land on one object. Non maximum suppression keeps the best box and discards the duplicates so each object appears once.

q: Compare image segmentation and object detection and give one situation where each is the better choice.
model: Segmentation classifies every pixel and gives a detailed mask with the exact shape and boundary of each object. It suits medical imaging and satellite analysis. Object detection draws bounding boxes and gives each a class label. It is coarser but faster, so it suits real time tasks such as finding pedestrians or vehicles. U-Net is a segmentation model, while YOLO is a detection model.
points: Segmentation gives pixel level masks and exact boundaries
Detection gives bounding boxes with class labels
Gives one use for each, such as medical imaging for segmentation and vehicle detection for detection

q: Explain how YOLO detects objects in an image, from input to final output.
model: YOLO resizes the image to a fixed shape, normalises the pixels and divides it into a grid. A CNN backbone extracts a feature map. Each grid cell predicts several bounding boxes with a confidence score and predicts class probabilities. Because the whole image is handled in one forward pass, YOLO is fast. Non maximum suppression then removes overlapping duplicates. The final output is a list of boxes, each with a class label and confidence score.
points: The image is resized, normalised and divided into a grid
A CNN backbone extracts a feature map
Each cell predicts boxes, confidence scores and classes
The output is boxes with class labels and confidence scores

q: Describe how non maximum suppression removes duplicate detections.
model: Several boxes can overlap the same object, so redundant boxes must be removed. All boxes are sorted by confidence score and the one with the highest score is kept. Each remaining box is compared with it using intersection over union. If the overlap is above a threshold, such as 0.5, the box is a duplicate and is discarded. If it is below the threshold the box is kept. The process repeats for the remaining boxes.
points: Many boxes may overlap one object
Sort by confidence and keep the highest
Compare others using intersection over union
Discard those above the threshold and keep those below
Repeat until all boxes are handled

q: Explain the differences between image classification, object detection and image segmentation. Describe the architecture and working principles of U-Net.
model: Image classification gives one label for the whole image. Object detection finds each object and gives it a class and a bounding box. Image segmentation labels every pixel, so it gives the exact shape of each region. Detection gives a coarser but faster result. U-Net is a network for segmentation with a U-shaped encoder and decoder. Contraction blocks of two 3x3 convolutions followed by 2x2 max pooling shrink the image and extract features. A bottleneck links the contraction and expansion paths. Expansion blocks of two 3x3 convolutions followed by 2x2 up-sampling rebuild the image size. Each expansion block receives a copy and crop of the matching contraction feature map. These skip connections restore spatial detail lost during pooling, and the output is a segmentation mask.
points: Classification gives one label per image
Detection gives classes and bounding boxes, segmentation labels each pixel
Contraction path of convolutions and max pooling
Expansion path of convolutions and up-sampling to rebuild size
Copy and crop skip connections restore detail lost in pooling

q: What is the main purpose of the skip connections between the encoder and decoder in U-Net?
options: To eliminate the need for convolutional operations
To transfer spatial information from encoder features to the matching decoder stages
To replace the output segmentation mask with a class label
To ensure that the network uses fewer trainable parameters
explain: Copy and crop passes encoder feature maps to the decoder, restoring detail lost during max pooling.

YOLO requires all images to contain exactly one object
YOLO predicts object locations and categories within an image
YOLO performs clustering before every prediction
